test_title: RRB Group D Official Paper (Held On: 26 Dec, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: Which of the following statements correctly explains the variety in the shape and size of cells?

options.text: The shape and size of cells are identical in plants and animals.
The shape and size of cells depend only on the availability of water.
The shape and size of all cells remain constant in every organism.
The shape and size of cells are related to the specific function they perform.

solution:
The correct answer is __**The shape and size of cells are related to the specific function they perform.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **shape** and **size** of cells are not uniform; they exhibit significant **diversity** depending on the **biological role** and **physiological requirements** of the organism. Cells are structured to maximize their **efficiency** in performing **specific functions**. ***Hence, statement 4 is correct.***
 
• While plants and animals share some basic cellular components, their **shape** and **size** are not identical. **Plant cells** typically have a fixed, **rectangular shape** due to the **cell wall**, whereas **animal cells** are often **irregular** or **round** and lack a cell wall. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.***
 
• The **morphology** of a cell is determined by **genetic factors** and **functional needs** rather than being solely dependent on the **availability of water**. Although **turgor pressure** (water content) affects cell volume, it is not the only deciding factor for **shape** and **size**. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.***
 
• The **shape** and **size** of cells do not remain constant; they vary across different **tissues** and **species**. For instance, a **nerve cell** is drastically different from a **skin cell** in the same organism, and **unicellular organisms** like **Amoeba** can even change their shape constantly. ***Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.***
 
• Specific examples of **functional adaptation** include **human nerve cells (neurons)**, which are **long and branched** to transmit **electrical impulses** over long distances, and **Red Blood Cells (RBCs)**, which are **biconcave** to increase **surface area** for **oxygen** transport.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Cell Size Variability:**
 
 
• The **smallest cell** known is **Mycoplasma** (a type of **bacteria**), measuring approximately **0.1 to 0.5 micrometers**.
 
• The **largest isolated single cell** is the **egg of an ostrich**, which can measure approximately **170 mm x 130 mm**.
 
• In the **human body**, the **smallest cell** is generally considered the **sperm cell**, while the **largest cell** is the **ovum (egg cell)**. The **longest cell** is the **nerve cell**.
 
 
 
• **Cell Shape Types:**
 
 
• Cells can be **spherical**, **spindle-shaped**, **elongated**, **cuboidal**, or **columnar**.
 
• **White Blood Cells (WBCs)** in humans are **amoeboid**, meaning they can **change shape** to squeeze through **capillary walls** and engulf **pathogens**.
 
• **Guard cells** in plant **stomata** are **kidney-shaped** or **bean-shaped** to regulate the opening and closing of pores for **gas exchange**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Discovery of the Cell:** The cell was first **discovered** and named by **Robert Hooke** in **1665** using a primitive **microscope** to observe **cork slices**.
 
• **Cell Theory:** Proposed by **Matthias Schleiden** and **Theodor Schwann** in **1838-39**, it states that all living things are composed of **cells**. **Rudolf Virchow** later added in **1855** that all cells arise from **pre-existing cells** (**Omnis cellula-e cellula**).
 
• **Functional Correlation:** The **surface area to volume ratio** is a critical factor limiting **cell size**. A smaller cell has a larger surface area relative to its **volume**, allowing for **faster diffusion** of **nutrients** and **waste**.
